7.4.1.6 Authenticated Encryption
Authenticated Encryption (
AE
) or Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (
AEAD
) provide confidentiality and data authenticity simultaneously.
AEAD
adds the abil-
ity to check the integrity and authenticity of some Associated Data (AD), also called ad-
ditional authenticated data. Additionally, this mechanism adds an
Message Authen-
tication Code
(
MAC
), as described in chapter 7.4.1.4, to conform that encrypted
data is authentic.
Note: the class
ara::crypto::cryp::AuthCipherCtx
provides authenticity and
confidentiality only for well known algorithm-protocols that derive both their prop-
erties from a single
Symmetric Key
(e.g. ChaCha20-Poly1305, aead/gimli24v1
or AES-GCM). To implement a custom authenticated-encryption protocol (follow-
ing a pattern of Encrypt-then-Mac, Mac-then-encrypt or Encrypt-and-Mac) the
classes
ara::crypto::cryp::StreamCipherCtx
and
ara::crypto::cryp::
MessageAuthnCodeCtx
can be used.
